claims.claim: David Mitchell states that the cumulative effect of Le Guin’s stylistic restraint is that A Wizard of Earthsea reads like a tale handed down through generations of storytellers.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: reads like the retelling of a tale first told centuries

claims.claim: David Mitchell states that a quoted passage describing an East Reach woman’s customary greeting gesture persuades precisely because its detail seems too particular to have been invented.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: Such specificity is persuasive because it sounds too detailed
claims.page: paragraph following the quoted East Reach greeting

claims.claim: David Mitchell names a studied neutrality of style as one of the two failure modes fantasy prose falls into, the other being a cod-historic narratorial voice.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: a studied neutrality of style tastes like clingfilm

claims.claim: David Mitchell states that a cod-historic narratorial voice in a fantasy novel feels like being locked inside a medieval theme park.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: A cod-historic narratorial voice in a fantasy novel

claims.claim: David Mitchell states that descriptions of people and places in A Wizard of Earthsea are frugal enough to leave the reader’s imagination room to collaborate.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: rich enough to nourish the reader’s imagination, but frugal enough

claims.claim: David Mitchell states that Le Guin gives minor characters who appear only briefly the psychological depth of oil paintings.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: thumbnail sketches contain the psychological depth of oil paintings

claims.claim: David Mitchell lists trade-routes, local politics, class hierarchies, infant mortality, abuse, addiction and slavery as the mundane institutional furniture that makes Earthsea’s fantastical elements feel quotidian.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: trade-routes, local politics, class hierarchies, infant mortality, abuse, addiction and slavery
claims.page: paragraph beginning "Earthsea is a fantasy world"

claims.claim: David Mitchell states that A Wizard of Earthsea contains moments of foreshadowing and authorial omniscience but no tricks.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: moments of foreshadowing and authorial omniscience but no tricks

claims.claim: Margaret Atwood names graceful prose first among the qualities that earned Le Guin her awards.
claims.source: Margaret Atwood, "The Queen of Quinkdom", The New York Review of Books, 26 September 2002 issue
claims.quote: her graceful prose, carefully thought-through premises, psychological insight
claims.page: paragraph beginning "Which brings us to Ursula K. Le Guin"

claims.claim: Margaret Atwood describes the task of Le Guin’s Ekumen envoys as non-invasive, non-directive understanding and recording of the societies they visit.
claims.source: Margaret Atwood, "The Queen of Quinkdom", The New York Review of Books, 26 September 2002 issue
claims.quote: non-directive understanding and recording are the functions required

claims.claim: Margaret Atwood states that Le Guin, though at times a movingly lyrical writer, has never avoided writing gore when the story required it.
claims.source: Margaret Atwood, "The Queen of Quinkdom", The New York Review of Books, 26 September 2002 issue
claims.quote: at times a movingly lyrical writer
claims.page: paragraph on "Old Music and the Slave Women"

claims.claim: The unsigned Kirkus review of Tehanu calls the novel’s prose flawless and poetic and says even young readers will be beguiled by it.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, unsigned review of Tehanu, 1 February 1990
claims.quote: beguiled by the flawless, poetic prose

claims.claim: The unsigned Kirkus review of Tehanu says Le Guin weaves contemporary concerns into a tale carrying the universality and dignity of legend.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, unsigned review of Tehanu, 1 February 1990
claims.quote: a tale with the universality and dignity of legend

claims.claim: Zadie Smith, in the Library of America tribute page, calls Le Guin’s sentences as elegant and beautiful as any written in the twentieth century.
claims.source: Zadie Smith, in "Fellow writers remember Ursula K. Le Guin, 1929–2018", Library of America, January 2018
claims.quote: her sentences, as elegant and beautiful as any written

claims.claim: Harold Bloom, in the Library of America tribute page, calls Le Guin an exquisite stylist.
claims.source: Harold Bloom, in "Fellow writers remember Ursula K. Le Guin, 1929–2018", Library of America, January 2018
